### 1. What the user expresses and how the simulator behaves

- Target object: "your 12-month CD … just matured and is going to roll over" — if asked, "the one ending in 4092" (unique). Source: "if asked which money market, it ends in 5174" (unique savings).
- Action boundary: "put in just enough from your money market for the CD to get the jumbo rate when it renews - not a penny more than it needs". Heard threshold "a hundred thousand dollars". Timing: now; renewal itself is future.
- Authorisation: "The bank can handle its own side however it has to; you will move the money out of the money market yourself once the agent sets it up and tells you the amount."
- Simulator passive/conditional: confirms the 6000.00 grace withdrawal only if raised; confirms Interest Checking 4861 as the interest destination only if asked; accepts a credit-back; executes the handed-over deposit tool with exactly the given values; accepts any amount as long as it comes from the money market. It pushes no step.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root P0: grace top-up sized to reach the Jumbo Bonus threshold on renewal ("just enough").

Hop P0 ← P1 (grace penalty credit-back must precede the sizing). **derived**.
- Chain: doc "The Ledger Figure a Grace Top-Up Is Measured Against": "a gap is never measured from a figure that still carries such a penalty. Since the Principal is read off the ledger, that credit is part of it only once it stands there as a reversal entry." Whether this penalty is "such a penalty" requires combining doc "Dating a Penalized Withdrawal to the Grace Period" (posted day 4), doc "When a Grace-Period Withdrawal Counts as the Owner's Own" (destination = owner's Interest Checking), doc "The Penalty Entry and Withdrawal Examined …" (latest entry, not reversed), doc "Penalties Charged on Money Taken Out During a Grace Period" ("It is credited back to the certificate with the adjustment reason of bank error") with the ledger (withdrawal labelled `early_partial`, penalty posted 2026-09-14). Arithmetic: gap 5773.39 without the credit vs 5714.66 with it; the customer's "not a penny more" matches the latter. No single sentence names the grace credit-back as coming before the top-up.

Hop P0 ← P2 (interest disposition repointing must precede the top-up). **derived**.
- Chain: doc "Grace Add-Ons and the Account Named for Interest Payouts": grace money is taken "only for as long as the interest disposition on the certificate points at no payout account that has been closed … for as long as it does, no top-up is written"; doc "When a Grace Top-Up Is Written …" lists "its interest disposition names no closed payout account". Record: disposition pay_to_checking, payout 06e08f86 = Everyday Checking closed 2026-08-05 (doc "Establishing That an Interest Payout Account Has Been Closed"). The state is changed only by a different policy: doc "Interest Payouts Directed to a Closed Account" (bank-owed repointing, tool `update_interest_disposition_67b383bc`) and doc "The Account That Takes Over Paid-Out Interest" (same-kind active account). Combining: the top-up is nothing until the repointing is recorded. The blocked-side sentence states the state condition, not the other policy's action; which action removes the condition must be found and combined. Marked derived (the closest-to-explicit sentence in this tree; see explicitness scan).

P1 ↔ P2: independent (one changes ledger/principal, the other the interest setting/payout account). Derived; no visible sentence states their relative order.

Leaves: no renewal (not owed until after 2026-09-20); maturity instruction auto_renew needs nothing; no other penalty.

Dependency direction and order: {P1, P2} (either order) -> P0.

Findability by record words: the governing docs are reachable by the words on the records ("grace period", "penalty", "payout account", "closed", "interest disposition", "Jumbo Bonus").

No document in the corpus describes this task's combination (grace withdrawal penalty + closed interest payout account + jumbo top-up) as a situation or workflow; the single workflow document in the corpus concerns a different situation (post-grace renewal with in-term add-on).

### Two-way counter-proof

- Support: all values fixed by quoted sentences + tool records; dry run reached the stated terminal state.
- Closest alternatives excluded:
  - Sizing from the record balance 94226.61 (gap 5773.39): excluded by "a gap is never measured from a figure that still carries such a penalty".
  - Treating the penalty under the rate/days mismatch rule: excluded — in-grace penalty stands outside that test; and its rate/days match anyway.
  - Declining the credit because the entry is labelled early_partial: excluded — "The dating rule looks only at the posting date".
  - Top-up refused because disposition names a closed account, with no repoint: excluded — the repoint is owed by the bank regardless of the owner.
  - Repointing to compounding or to the savings account: excluded — owner has an active account of the same kind (checking) -> stays pay_to_checking to Interest Checking.
  - Booking the renewal now: excluded — renewal not owed until the day after the last grace day.
  - In-term add-on tool instead of grace add-on: excluded — 12-Month tier allows 0 in-term add-ons; certificate is in grace.
  - Trimming to savings balance: not triggered (7420.66 ≥ 5714.66).
- Wrong answer "do only the one thing asked" (hand over the grace deposit at 5773.39 or at any sum): excluded by visible principles — with the interest disposition pointing at the closed Everyday Checking, "no top-up is written, whatever the size of the gap"; and a gap measured before the owed credit-back posts is a figure "that still carries such a penalty". Both exclusions follow by combining sentences; neither is stated as an instruction.

### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

- object — "the certificate of deposit she keeps at Piedmont Crescent", known to her only as "the last four digits on the statement, 2058 … she has no other reference numbers and would not know where to look for them";
- target — "to put the certificate back where it was, to top it up so it is whole again for the rest of its term", and "she would rather do it in one go than dribble it back";
- boundary on the amount — she supplies none: "that is the question she is asking them: whatever it takes to make the certificate whole for the term, worked out properly"; "If she is pressed for a figure she says she would rather not guess";
- funding — "The money is sitting in her account at the credit union and she will send it over as a transfer, not a check and not cash";
- authorisation — she executes it: "When the representative hands the deposit over for her to make herself, she goes through with it there and then".

The simulator is passive: "She answers questions and otherwise waits", "She never suggests what the bank should do first, never offers a number of her own". She names the Premier Checking, the savings opened in March, the car loan and the Visa **only when asked** — "She sees no connection between any of that and the certificate and does not press the point". On the hidden work she is explicitly non-directive: "If the representative tells her that something was left off the certificate's record and has to be put right before the top-up can be worked out, she says that is exactly why she called them … and lets them get on with it" — a conditional response to something the agent has already worked out, never a hint.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure rests on a quoted document sentence plus a quoted record field.

**The closest alternatives, and the visible sentence that excludes each.**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Book the charge against the **2026-02-19** withdrawal too | `charges_owed_on_principal_taken_out` opening: the charge is owed where the ledger shows a withdrawal "with no charge standing against that withdrawal". The 166.83 `cd_penalty` row's `source_item_id` names `606b2279-…`, so that one stands charged. |
| Work the charge on both withdrawals' principal (14500.00) | `working_out_the_charge_owed` §1: "worked out on the principal taken out … **in the three months before the day the entry is booked**"; 2026-02-19 is outside 2026-04-08→2026-07-08. |
| Reverse the missing penalty instead of booking it | `reversing_an_early_withdrawal_penalty` §1 governs a penalty **assessed** and reversed on bank error or the death waiver; here no penalty was assessed at all — the opposite case. |
| Set the loss at the bare principal removed, 14500.00 | `principal_a_term_has_lost` first grade, whose conditions (auto loan not past due; more than one withdrawal in the twelve months) both hold on the records. |
| Run the interest over the whole term, or from 2026-02-19 | `spans_of_restored_interest` first grade: "from the day the **last** sum left to the day of the deposit"; the second grade's term-start span is reserved to a single withdrawal. |
| Round the deposit to the nearest cent (15375.79) | `rounding_of_restoring_deposits` first grade, both conditions holding. |
| Split the top-up over several deposits | `in_term_add_on_limits`: the tier accepts **1** deposit in a term; and she asks to do it "in one go". |
| Take the money from a Piedmont Crescent account | She names the credit-union transfer and confirms it; `restoring_a_term_to_its_opening_principal` §4 defines `external_ach` for exactly that. |
| `adjustment_reason 'none'` | §3 reserves **none** for "an ordinary charge raised under the certificate's own terms **rather than a correction of the bank's own records**", and reads **bank_error** onto "a charge the bank failed to raise at the time". |

**Excluding "she asked for only one thing, so do only that one thing."** Fixing the deposit without first booking the owed charge leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles do not allow: `restoring_a_term_to_its_opening_principal` §2 says in terms that while an early partial withdrawal stands with no entry against it, "the deposit is not yet in a state to be fixed" — and `find_cd_transactions` shows `e6862990-…` standing exactly so. The exclusion rests on the blocked policy's own prerequisite sentence and a ledger scan, not on any statement naming the other problem, its tool or an order between them.
